advances: In the canonical normalized empty-full branch, the two exact diagonal support contacts and midpoint inclusion force the transformed copy of \(A_0\) into a rectangle of area \(4\alpha\beta\). Hence \(M\le 2\alpha\beta\). This establishes only the contact-box bound and makes no reverse claim from \(\Phi(G)<0\).
author: mp_r99_support_contact_box
proof:
First recover the two contacts from the normalized empty-full support statement. For the diagonal crossing with affine function
\[
\psi_u(x,y)=-(x+y),
\]
the normalized crossing level is \(L_u=0\). Accepted fact `624b129b68e0fdee` states in an empty-full lower crossing that \(L_u=-\max_{A_2}\psi_u\). Thus \(\max_{A_2}\psi_u=0\). The same argument with
\[
\psi_v(x,y)=y-x
\]
and \(L_v=0\) gives \(\max_{A_2}\psi_v=0\). These are exactly (1). Since \(A_2\subseteq\mathcal R\), both functions are nonpositive on \(A_2\). Compactness therefore gives points \(a_u,a_v\in A_2\) such that
\[
x(a_u)+y(a_u)=0,\qquad x(a_v)-y(a_v)=0.
\]
Writing
\[
q_u=D(a_u),\qquad q_v=D(a_v),
\]
we have
\[
(q_u)_u=0,\qquad(q_v)_v=0.
\tag{5}
\]
Accepted fact `eddda25c734d34bc` audits precisely the one-sided support cases behind this conclusion: a maximizing edge has a positive interior trace, while a maximizing vertex has zero trace and the first nonzero affine-chord slope. In either case the maximizing face itself is present and (5) is exact. Thus if
\[
F_u=Q\cap\{u=0\},\qquad F_v=Q\cap\{v=0\},
\]
then each \(F_u,F_v\) is a nonempty exposed face. Because \(Q\) is a two-dimensional polygon, each is either a vertex or a nondegenerate edge. The faces may meet at the vertex \((0,0)\), in which case one point supplies both choices in (5).

The coordinate map sends the two diagonal cones exactly to the two coordinate quadrants:
\[
D(\mathcal L)=(-\infty,0]^2,\qquad
D(\mathcal R)=[0,\infty)^2.
\]
The additional central reflection in the definition of \(P\) therefore gives
\[
P,Q\subseteq[0,\infty)^2.
\tag{6}
\]
For arbitrary \(p\in P\) and \(q\in Q\), choose \(a_0\in A_0\) and \(a_2\in A_2\) with
\[
p=-D(a_0),\qquad q=D(a_2).
\]
Linearity and the midpoint inclusion give
\[
\frac{q-p}{2}
=D\left(\frac{a_0+a_2}{2}\right)\in D(K)=K'.
\tag{7}
\]
Fix \(p\in P\). Applying (7) first with \(q=q_u\), and using the definition \(\min_{K'}u=-\alpha\), yields
\[
-\frac{p_u}{2}
=\left(\frac{q_u-p}{2}\right)_u
\ge-\alpha,
\qquad\text{so}\qquad p_u\le2\alpha.
\tag{8}
\]
Applying (7) with \(q=q_v\) similarly gives
\[
-\frac{p_v}{2}
=\left(\frac{q_v-p}{2}\right)_v
\ge-\beta,
\qquad\text{so}\qquad p_v\le2\beta.
\tag{9}
\]
Together with (6), these inequalities prove the box inclusion in (2). They are non-strict, so points and edges on any boundary of the box cause no exception.

The matrix of \(D\) is
\[
\begin{pmatrix}1&1\\1&-1\end{pmatrix},
\]
whose determinant is \(-2\). The reflection used to define \(P\) has area factor \(1\). Consequently
\[
|P|=2|A_0|=2M.
\tag{10}
\]
The box inclusion and (10) now give
\[
2M=|P|\le(2\alpha)(2\beta)=4\alpha\beta,
\]
which is the claimed \(M\le2\alpha\beta\).

The same argument also audits degeneracy. Equations (6), (8), and (9) imply \(\alpha,\beta\ge0\). If \(\alpha=0\), then \(P\subseteq\{u=0\}\), contradicting \(|P|=2M>0\); similarly \(\beta\ne0\). Hence \(\alpha,\beta>0\), so the containing box is nondegenerate.

Finally, equality \(M=2\alpha\beta\) is equivalent by (10) to \(P\) having the full area of its containing box. Since \(P\) is compact, any point of the box omitted by \(P\) would have a relative neighborhood of positive area disjoint from \(P\). Thus equality forces (3), and (3) plainly suffices. Applying \(a_0=D^{-1}(-p)\) to the four corners of (3) gives exactly the four vertices in (4). In particular, equality is allowed on the diagonal boundaries: the two edges of \(P\) on \(u=0\) and \(v=0\) become edges of \(A_0\) on the two boundary rays of \(\mathcal L\). No strict-containment assumption, positive-length support face, or separation of the two contact points was used.
statement:
Let
\[
\mathcal L=\{(x,y)\in\mathbb R^2:x\le-|y|\},
\qquad
\mathcal R=\{(x,y)\in\mathbb R^2:x\ge|y|\}.
\]
Let \(A_0,A_2,K\subset\mathbb R^2\) be nonempty compact two-dimensional convex polygons such that
\[
A_0\subseteq\mathcal L,\qquad A_2\subseteq\mathcal R,\qquad
\frac{A_0+A_2}{2}\subseteq K,
\qquad
M:=|A_0|\ge |A_2|>0.
\]
Assume the two mandatory maximizing-support conditions furnished in the canonical normalized empty-full case by accepted facts `624b129b68e0fdee` and `eddda25c734d34bc`:
\[
\max_{(x,y)\in A_2}(-(x+y))=0,
\qquad
\max_{(x,y)\in A_2}(y-x)=0.
\tag{1}
\]
Define the invertible linear map
\[
D(x,y)=(u,v)=(x+y,x-y),
\qquad
D^{-1}(u,v)=\left(\frac{u+v}{2},\frac{u-v}{2}\right),
\]
and put
\[
P=-D(A_0),\qquad Q=D(A_2),\qquad K'=D(K),
\]
\[
\alpha=-\min_{z\in K'}z_u,\qquad
\beta=-\min_{z\in K'}z_v.
\]
Then
\[
P\subseteq[0,2\alpha]\times[0,2\beta],
\qquad
M\le2\alpha\beta.
\tag{2}
\]
The conclusion is unchanged whether either maximizing face in (1) is a vertex or an edge, including when both contacts are the same vertex. Moreover \(\alpha,\beta>0\), and equality in (2) holds if and only if
\[
P=[0,2\alpha]\times[0,2\beta].
\tag{3}
\]
Equivalently, the equality case for \(A_0\) is
\[
A_0=\operatorname{conv}\{(0,0),(-\alpha,-\alpha),
(-\beta,\beta),(-\alpha-\beta,\beta-\alpha)\}.
\tag{4}
\]
